text.p: Teva Pharmaceutical Industries Ltd declared a regular quarterly cash dividend of about 6.2 cents per American depositary receipt (ADR) to be paid on December 9.
Earlier on Monday, the Israeli company reported higher third-quarter earnings.
The company said in a statement that price erosion trends resulting from increased competition continued in all of the company's major markets.
"The penetration of new products and increased unit sales of existing products balanced out the erosion and contributed to an improvement of the company's gross profit margins," the statement said.
In the third quarter sales in Israel rose 9.7 percent to $72.5 million, representing 30 percent of Teva's total revenue base.
Sales outside of Israel in the quarter were $164.1 million, up 21.6 percent from a year earlier.
North America remains Teva's largest market, representing close to half its revenues with sales essentially flat year to year for the third quarter.
Pharmaceutical sales amounted to $183.4 million in the quarter and accounted for 77 percent of total sales. Bulk pharmaceutical chemical sales grew 36 percent to $27.2 million in the third quarter.
Gross profit in the third quarter rose to $92.4 million from $72.1 million a year earlier, representing a margin improvement of 300 basis points, the company said.

Net research and development expenses, after grants, rose 59.8 percent in the quarter to $14.9 million, reflecting a lower level of grants received from the Chief Scientist's Office in Israel, the statement said.
